title: Game Theory
tagline: Strategic-form games and dominance, Nash equilibrium, mixed strategies, continuous games, extensive-form games and subgame perfection, bargaining, repeated games, Bayesian games and signalling
summary: Game theory is the mathematics of strategic interaction: situations in which each decision-maker’s best choice depends on what the others do. This course develops the core solution concepts — dominance, Nash equilibrium in pure and mixed strategies, subgame-perfect equilibrium, and equilibria of repeated and Bayesian games — and applies them to coordination, the commons, bargaining, cooperation, auctions and signalling.

chapters.title: Strategic-form games and dominance
chapters.summary: Players, strategies and payoffs, dominant and dominated strategies, and iterated elimination of dominated strategies.

chapters.title: Nash equilibrium
chapters.summary: Best responses, Nash equilibrium in pure strategies, and applications to coordination, conflict and the provision of public goods.

chapters.title: Mixed strategies
chapters.summary: Randomised strategies, the indifference principle, the existence of equilibrium, and zero-sum games with the minimax theorem.

chapters.title: Games with continuous strategies
chapters.summary: Best-response functions with continuous actions, existence by fixed points, and applications to location, contests and the tragedy of the commons.

chapters.title: Extensive-form games and backward induction
chapters.summary: Game trees, strategies in sequential games, backward induction and subgame-perfect equilibrium.

chapters.title: Bargaining
chapters.summary: The Nash bargaining solution and Rubinstein’s model of alternating offers.

chapters.title: Repeated games and cooperation
chapters.summary: Finitely and infinitely repeated games, trigger strategies, the folk theorem and when cooperation can be sustained.

chapters.title: Games of incomplete information
chapters.summary: Types and beliefs, Bayesian Nash equilibrium, and applications to auctions and voluntary contributions.

chapters.title: Perfect Bayesian equilibrium and signalling
chapters.summary: Beliefs on and off the equilibrium path, signalling games, pooling and separating equilibria, and cheap talk.
